rules.interval: paired log ratios ln(C/B); n=12 -> one-based order statistics r(3), r(10); n=24 -> r(7), r(18) (analyze_bc_qualification.summarize_metric, unchanged)
rules.classification: PASS if upper <= ln(1+t); REGRESSION if lower > ln(1+t); else INCONCLUSIVE. For higher-is-better metrics the ratio is B/C. IMPROVED is reported (never claimed otherwise) only when the upper bound is below 0.
rules.A: v0.4.0 rules unchanged (analyze_bc_qualification.evaluate_cell, final decision), FIXED n = 24 pairs per cell (plan section 5.3, option a): two blocks of 12 pairs per cell (session seeds, then extension seeds), both always run for all nine cells; no analysis between the blocks and no extension rule; the 24 pairs of a cell form one sample (block recorded, not a stratum, not weighted); interval [r(7), r(18)], coverage 1 - 2 P(Bin(24, 1/2) <= 6) = 0.9773; INCONCLUSIVE_DISCLOSED only for an INCONCLUSIVE primary with median <= t and every supporting metric PASS; a primary INCONCLUSIVE with median > t is REGRESSION; else UNRESOLVED (analyze_v100q_a.py, run once after block 2)
rules.B_C: v0.5.0 protocol sections 3-4 unchanged (tolerances 25/50/100/6%, B5 3.0x, C1-C4); lifecycle scope compact-bfs; window multipliers of run 4 (window-multipliers-dcd8ccc.json) reused unchanged so cells are identical to v0.5.0's; no extension, no rerun
rules.R: 12 analyzed pairs after 2 discarded warmup pairs, fresh process per observation, arm order balanced 6/6 within the analyzed pairs by a seeded shuffle (order seed experiments.R.order_seed); no extension; tolerance primary 10%
rules.Rmem: deterministic allocator byte counts, one run per arm; REGRESSION if candidate > reference x 1.20, otherwise PASS; reported with absolute values
rules.M_desc: descriptive, no verdict; each configuration record classified VALID/INVALID by the validity rule; M5 rule (i) of the v0.6.0 design is re-evaluated descriptively (mean graph-lock wait of the batch job >= 50% of mean client latency for read95/read100 at 16 or 64 closed-loop clients without background activity)
rules.M_reg: 12 analyzed pairs after 2 warmup pairs, a fresh server process per observation, arm order balanced; throughput tolerance primary 10% (ratio B/C), client p99 tolerance query_tail 25%
rules.no_waiver_inheritance: No maintainer waiver or acceptance from v0.6.0 or earlier applies. Every v0.6.0 non-PASS cell (R HTTP import 60/30 REGRESSION, B4 import-high REGRESSION, C3 FAIL x3, A UNRESOLVED x2, INCONCLUSIVE(_DISCLOSED) cells, C4 disclosures) is re-measured under the same rules and reported as measured. This applies equally to the first v0.7.0 campaign: none of its results is accepted, pooled or used to choose cells.
rules.validity: a configuration record is VALID only if errors == 0, item_errors is empty, noop_mutations == 0 and, with background activity, background.failures == 0 and background.completed > 0. 503 refusals are allowed and reported (admission limit 32 pending jobs). For M_reg every analyzed observation must also have only status 200 (unchanged analyzer). An invalid record is reported as invalid, never rerun or dropped; an M_reg cell with any invalid analyzed observation gets no verdict (INVALID).
rules.probe: contention-probe revision 2 (fixes of the v0.6.0 M supplement): KNOTREL_MAX_NODES = nodes + 100000, current ETag for imports, 503 feeder refusals retried after 10 ms and counted, per-item errors and no-op mutations counted, fresh extra-edge IDs per configuration

T5.same_duration_and_workload: within a topology every run has the same schedule digest, result digest, calls per cycle, final logical counts and compaction cycles; otherwise the analysis is invalid

metrics.P_max: longest single lifecycle call of the run
metrics.P_90: 27th of the 30 sorted per-interval maxima; interval k = the cycles after compaction k-1 up to and including compaction k; exactly 30 compactions, the last at cycle 600, else invalid

T5.aggregation: per pair d = ln(C/B) for each metric
T5.interval: [d(3), d(10)] of the 12 sorted d: distribution-free interval for the median of d, coverage 96.1%; point estimate median of d
T5.tolerance_basis: a new criterion for pause tails, declared before collection; not inherited from query_tail
T5.rule: PASS if d(10) <= ln(1.25); REGRESSION if d(3) > ln(1.25); otherwise INCONCLUSIVE; for each metric and topology (six deciding results); any non-PASS goes to the maintainer, no waiver
T5.invalid: a failed run stops the collector (chain FAILED); a validation failure of the analysis leaves T5 without PASS
T5.absolute_values: reported for every result: per arm median, minimum and maximum of each metric, wall and timed run durations, mean call time
T5.perimeter: excluded unless the core rule triggers (v1_0_0.core_rule); its definition is kept unchanged for that case

invalidation.code_change: any change to executed code of knotrel after freezing invalidates every experiment that ran that code; documentation-only commits do not (executed code identity is checked by comparing __TEXT,__text of release builds)
invalidation.tooling_change: any change to a probe, collector or analysis after freezing invalidates the affected experiment
invalidation.failed_child: a failing child stops the experiment; one rerun only for an infrastructure failure unrelated to the measured code, recorded with its cause
invalidation.invalid_runs: kept and reported; never deleted or overwritten (collectors refuse to overwrite)
invalidation.conformance: see conformance.outcome; conformance failures are not infrastructure failures and do not use the one-rerun allowance

budget.basis: plan section 9: v0.9.0 attempt 2 durations (A main block 998.0 s and a 12-pair block of 108 pairs about 940 s; whole BC 637.5 s; R 156.4 s; Rmem 11.2 s; M_reg 818.3 s) plus the quiet, grace and gate overhead; about 86 minutes if the core rule adds T5 (949.7 s) and the full BC
budget.caps: two separate caps, not a shared pool: Part 1 (A, B4+C, R, Rmem, M_reg and their conformance overhead) <= 105 minutes; Q (including the Q5 reference arm) <= 30 minutes; time left in one cap is never carried to the other

exceeded.part1: BUDGET EXHAUSTED: the chain stops; the attempt is NONCONFORMING (no Part 1 verdict, data kept); a second attempt under the attempts rule, never Q's minutes; Q does not run
exceeded.q: the run stops and keeps the completed observations; block Q is NONCONFORMING: criteria whose cells lack their three observations get no verdict and none counts as PASS; Q can be rerun once, as a whole, only for this non-conformance or an infrastructure failure, never because of a result; a second non-conforming Q goes to the maintainer; Part 1 is unaffected

conformance.rule: Nothing outside the allow-list runs, and no user input occurs, from the start of the quiet period to the end of the chain.

classes.order: campaign; zombie -> class of its parent; new controller descendant -> forbidden; PID 0 -> system; deny_basenames -> forbidden; foreground app other than Finder and the Claude desktop app -> forbidden; controller and the chain's ancestors below it -> baseline; Claude desktop app -> baseline; unresolvable live process -> forbidden; Apple-controlled location or system app extension -> system; host_baseline -> baseline; otherwise forbidden
classes.campaign: the chain process and its descendants (PID ancestry)
classes.system: PID 0, or an executable under /System/Library/, /System/Cryptexes/, /System/iOSSupport/System/Library/, /System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/, /usr/libexec/, /usr/sbin/, /sbin/, /usr/bin/, /bin/, /Library/Apple/, or a system app extension /System/Applications/*.app/Contents/PlugIns/*.appex/; never invalidates; CPU time reported
classes.baseline: the controlling Claude Code CLI (validated: a Claude Code CLI executable and an ancestor of the chain) and the chain's ancestors below it; the Claude desktop app (/Applications/Claude.app/); the executables in host_baseline; CPU time reported
classes.forbidden: any other live descendant of the controller at policy time (launch refused) or later (a tool call); any executable on deny_basenames (for an unresolvable process, the comm base name); any registered foreground app (lsappinfo) other than Finder and the Claude desktop app; any unresolvable live process; every process not in the classes above

conformance.host_baseline_note: privileged background helpers that stay resident after their apps quit (inventory of 2026-11-17, scripts/conformance_monitor.py inventory). Any other resident non-system process found at preparation needs a matrix amendment and a new freeze before measuring; it is never allowed silently.
conformance.user_input: HID idle time (ioreg IOHIDSystem HIDIdleTime), read once per second by the monitor and at every gate check, timestamped with the monotonic clock at the read; input is a reading below previous + elapsed - hid_tolerance_s
conformance.liveness: monitor samples the full process table every 0.2 s, writes a heartbeat per sample, and exits if the chain process disappears; gate before every child: monitor PID alive, status age <= 1.0 s, zero violation/HID-reset/HID-failure totals; gate after every child: heartbeats covering the child with no gap > 1.0 s; at chain end: the same over the whole attempt from the quiet-period start
conformance.git_state: read-only snapshot (FETCH_HEAD mtime, remote-tracking reflog sizes) of every clone under /Users/rt/workspace/knotrel before the quiet period and after the chain; any difference is forbidden activity
conformance.cpu_accounting: per child, CPU seconds of system, baseline and forbidden classes from cumulative ps CPU time; disclosure only, no threshold
conformance.outcome: any failed check stops the chain at the next gate and makes the whole attempt NONCONFORMING (no verdict for any experiment of the attempt, completed ones included); data kept; every exit path writes logs/CONFORMANCE.txt, the final Git state and checksums; restart only after the cause is removed, into a new directory, with the same frozen matrix and seeds; at most 3 attempts, then the maintainer decides; amendment 1: a new series a1 with its own cap (conformance.amendment_1.attempts_cap), the first CONFORMING attempt is final; amendment 2: series a1 closed with zero attempts; a new series a2 with its own cap (conformance.amendment_2.attempts_cap), the first CONFORMING attempt is final; amendment 3: series a2 closed with zero attempts; a new series a3 (conformance.amendment_3.attempts_cap), no soak, the first CONFORMING attempt is final
conformance.limits: a process that starts and exits between two 0.2 s samples can be missed (CPU accounting and the Git snapshot cover such processes in part); tool calls that start no process are covered only by the transcript check; allowed system processes are not limited in CPU; root-writable firmlinked data directories under /System/Library and /usr/libexec are treated as system; PIDs are not paired with start times (the baseline PIDs are the chain's own ancestors, alive throughout); a SIGTERM to the chain alone takes effect when the current collector ends (the attempt is still NONCONFORMING); rare system dialogs registered as foreground apps (for example Problem Reporter) stop the attempt
conformance.grace_period: between launch and the policy: the operator leaves the Mac and the controller ends its turn; not monitored; at its end the session must be stable for session_stable_s and the HID idle time at least min_hid_idle_at_policy_s, or the launch is refused (NOT STARTED, no attempt consumed)
conformance.controller_transcript: the launch is refused unless the given transcript is under ~/.claude/projects/, was modified in the last 600 s and contains the run_final_chain.sh launch for this campaign; after the grace period, the size and mtime of the transcript and of every file in its session directory (subagent transcripts) must be unchanged for session_stable_s (else the launch is refused); the same state is compared after every step and at chain end, and any change makes the attempt NONCONFORMING
conformance.gating_verification: at chain end, every child each collector recorded must have exactly one conforming gate record (A observations, B/C cells, R/Rmem/M_desc/M_reg children); B/C gates exactly the three declared probe binaries and refuses any other absolute-path program

E' un laptop non un server dedicato', then delegated the choices: 'Scegli tu quello che ci aiuta a portare risultati sensati ma anche a non restare bloccati per giorni'. The choices below were made by the controller under that delegation
amendment_3.cause: no run so far was conforming: attempt 1 (original series) stopped on user input (quiet period, HID reset); attempt 2 on the WhatsApp notification extension (57 monitor violations); attempt 3 on GoogleUpdater (74 violations); soak a1-1 on one git process spawned by the Claude Code CLI (1 violation); soak a2-2 on Safari's CacheDeleteExtension caught at startup with no resolvable path (1 violation, rule 8). The host preparation of amendments 1 and 2 removed the persistent causes; the remaining failures were single samples of benign processes, and an allow-list that forbids every unknown process is not workable on a laptop over hours
amendment_3.changes: rules 8 (unresolvable live process) and 11 (any other process) give the new class background (allowed, CPU recorded) instead of forbidden; still forbidden, also when unresolved or shown as '(name)': new Terminal descendants, deny-listed executables (parentheses stripped, a 16-character cut name matched by prefix) plus the non-campaign interpreters Python and node, foreground apps other than Finder and Terminal, any Claude executable (path, a name starting with claude, or a command line naming claude-code, scanned once a second); the launcher audit is recorded, not a precondition; no soak; still checked: HID input, Git state, ~/.claude/projects, monitor liveness and the per-child gate; quiesce and restore of the updaters unchanged; experiments, seeds, statistics, thresholds and analyzers unchanged
amendment_3.interference: disclosure only, no invalidation. Recorded: each gate child record's cpu_seconds_by_class (system, baseline, background) from ps CPU totals before and after the child, which misses processes that start and exit within the child (under-count, disclosed); the monitor's per-second top record adds background_pcpu_sum (sum of ps %CPU of background processes in that sample), which does see short-lived processes alive at a sample. Reported (specified now, implemented in the comparison report before the analysis, not part of the frozen tooling): per cell, background and baseline CPU as a share of one core over the child's duration, and the mean background_pcpu_sum over the child; cells above 25% of one core on either measure are marked 'read with caution'
amendment_3.closed_series: a2: zero attempts (soak a2-2 SOAK NONCONFORMING; soak budget exhausted); recorded and reported
amendment_3.soak: none required under amendment 3 (its purpose was to show that no unknown process runs, which amendment 3 no longer requires)

amendment_3.review: independent review of the delta before the freeze (controller's choice under the delegation)
amendment_3.cli_differences: policy.json and the monitor start record gain background_allowed; the monitor's top records gain background_pcpu_sum; the monitor runs ps -Ao pid=,args= at most once a second (claude_pids_cached)

infrastructure_failure.definition: only if all three hold: unrelated to the measured code; recorded with evidence (log line, system event, time); one of: a host power or thermal event (pmset), disk full or a filesystem error, loss of the local PostgreSQL container or its loopback network (container exit, docker error, refused connection to PostgreSQL), a crash of the tooling outside the product (collector, harness, load tool, monitor) not caused by a product response, an operating-system kill not caused by the product's memory use
infrastructure_failure.allowance: one rerun of that child (invalidation.failed_child) or, in Q, of that observation, recorded with its cause; a second failure of the same child is final

product_failure.rule: a crash or panic of knotrel-server, knotrel-core or the probe's in-process router, a timeout, a wrong result, a validation failure or an unexpected HTTP error is a result of that cell, never rerun automatically
product_failure.A_R_Rmem_B4_C: the child fails and the chain stops; the cell is FAIL; cells of that experiment that did not run get no verdict and are reported as not run (a C cell's C2 failure is FAIL by rule)
product_failure.M_reg: the observation is invalid and the cell is INVALID
product_failure.Q: the observation counts as measured, with its failure; a server crash, a feeder not ready within 300 s or a wrong answer gives the criteria using that observation no passing value, so they FAIL
product_failure.conformance: conformance failures are neither: they make the attempt NONCONFORMING and never use the rerun allowance
